part2.intro: Three young people talk about a sport they started recently.
part2.question: For each question, choose the correct answer.

texts.label: A
texts.title: Oliver
texts.text: I started playing golf last summer when my uncle took me to his club. I thought golf was a sport for old people, but I was wrong – there are lots of young players. I practise twice a week after school. Lessons are quite expensive, so I save my pocket money to pay for them. Next month I'm entering my first competition. I'm a bit nervous, but my coach says I'm ready.

texts.label: B
texts.title: Linh
texts.text: My brother taught me to play table-tennis in our garage at home. He's a member of a club in town, and now I go with him every Saturday. I love it because it's fast and you don't have to be tall or strong to be good at it. Last month I won a prize in a competition for girls under fourteen. My racket was a present from my brother – he bought it with his own money!

texts.label: C
texts.title: Sofia
texts.text: I joined the climbing club at the sports centre in January. At first I was scared because the climbing wall is fifteen metres high! But the coaches are really friendly and they always check that we're safe. Climbing makes my arms very tired, so I need a long rest afterwards. In the summer, the club goes climbing in the mountains, and I can't wait to try it outside.

part3.title: From last place to the finish line
part3.text:
Fourteen-year-old Ellie Brooks never liked sport. "At primary school I was always the last person in every race," she says. "I hated PE lessons, and I often forgot my trainers on purpose!"

Everything changed last spring when her older cousin, Jess, ran a marathon to get money for a children's hospital. Ellie went to watch her with the family. "There were thousands of runners of all ages, and lots of them weren't fast at all. But everybody was smiling. That's when I decided I wanted to try."

Ellie didn't want to run alone, so she asked her PE teacher, Mr Patel, if she could start a running club at school. He agreed, and now twenty students meet every Tuesday and Thursday before lessons. "We don't run very far – about three kilometres – and we talk all the time," Ellie laughs. "It isn't a competition. Nobody cares who the winner is."

The hardest part was getting up early. "In winter it's dark and cold at seven o'clock, and my bed is so warm! But my friends wait for me at the school gate, so I can't stay at home."

In September the club entered a five-kilometre fun run in the city park. Ellie finished in thirty-two minutes. "I wasn't first, but I didn't stop once. And my cousin was there with a big sign with my name on it!"

Next year Ellie wants to try a ten-kilometre race. "Who knows? Maybe one day I'll run a marathon like Jess."

options: She enjoyed PE but she wasn't fast.
She didn't like it at all.

options: She saw that the marathon runners were enjoying themselves.
Her cousin asked her to run a marathon with her.
She wanted to get money for a hospital.

items.q: Why does Ellie go to the club on winter mornings?
options: Her friends are waiting for her.
Her teacher gives prizes to people who come.
She enjoys running when it's dark.

items.q: What happened at the fun run?
options: Ellie ran all the way without stopping.
Ellie's cousin ran next to her.

part4.title: How basketball began
part4.text:
Basketball is one of the most popular sports in the world, but it is not very old. In 1891, a teacher in the USA called James Naismith wanted to {19} a new game for his students. It was winter, and it was too cold to play football outside, so he needed a sport that people could play {20}.

Naismith put two fruit baskets on the walls of the gym, and the students tried to {21} a ball into them. Every time a player scored, someone had to climb up and {22} the ball out of the basket! Later, people cut holes in the bottom of the baskets.

The first game had nine players in each team, but today there are only five. Basketball {23} part of the Olympic Games in 1936. Now millions of people play it in schools, parks and sports centres. You don't need much to {24} – just a ball, a basket and some friends!

items.q: Which sport will the girl play on Saturday?

script.t: Dad, can you drive me to the sports centre on Saturday morning?
For your swimming lesson?
No, the pool's closed this weekend. I'm playing volleyball with Anna's team. They need one more player.
Oh. I thought you were playing tennis with Grace this weekend.
That's on Sunday afternoon.

items.q: How much will the boy pay for his ticket?

script.t: Hello. How much are tickets for Saturday's hockey match?
Adult tickets are fifteen pounds.
I'm thirteen. Is it cheaper for me?
Yes. For under-sixteens it's eight pounds if you buy it now. If you buy it on the day of the match, it's twelve.
OK, I'll buy one now, then.

items.q: What has the boy forgotten?

script.t: Have you got everything for your tennis lesson, Sam?
I think so. My racket's in my bag, and I'm wearing my trainers.
What about a drink? It's very hot today.
Oh no! I left my water bottle on the kitchen table.
Don't worry. You can buy one at the club.

items.q: Where is Lucas now?

script.t: Hi, is Lucas at home? We're going cycling this afternoon.
No, sorry. He went to the beach early this morning to go surfing.
Is he still there? Or is he at the pool? He sometimes has swimming practice on Saturdays.
Swimming's tomorrow. He phoned an hour ago – he's at the stadium with his dad now, watching the football. He'll be back at six.

items.q: Which sport does the boy want to try this winter?

script.t: Are you going skiing with your family again this winter, Minh?
Yes, we're going to the mountains in February. But I'm a bit bored of skiing. I've done it for years.
So will you go ice skating instead?
No, I'm not very good at that. I want to have snowboarding lessons. My cousin says it's easier than it looks.
Cool! Send me a video.

part2.intro: You will hear a man talking about a summer sports camp.
part2.title: Hillside Summer Sports Camp

script.t: Hello, everyone. I'm going to tell you about this year's Summer Sports Camp at Hillside Sports Centre. The camp is for young people aged ten to fifteen. It starts on Monday the twenty-first of July – not on the Saturday, as it said on our website. Sorry about that! Please arrive at a quarter to nine every morning. Activities start at nine o'clock, and we finish at four. There are lots of sports to choose from: tennis, basketball, swimming in the indoor pool, and this year we're adding baseball for the first time. A week at the camp costs ninety-five pounds. That includes lunch every day, but you'll need to bring your own drinks. If you're a member of the sports centre, it's only eighty pounds. On the last day, Friday, there'll be a big race around the park, and the winner will get a prize, so practise your running! Parents are welcome to come and watch. Please bring your swimming costume and a towel every day. If you have any questions, please contact the camp leader, Mrs Dalby. That's D-A-L-B-Y. Her email address is on the website.

items.q: How long is the race that Oscar is entering?
Where does Oscar ride his bike on Sundays?
Whose bike will Oscar use in the race?
What does Oscar hope to do in the race?
options: beat the riders from cycling clubs
finish in less than an hour

items.q: Where will Oscar's family watch the race?

script.t: Hi Oscar. Is it true you're entering the bike race next month?

Yes! It goes along the river from the town centre. My PE teacher told me about it. At first I wanted to do the ten-kilometre race, but my dad said I was ready for the twenty-kilometre one. There's a thirty-kilometre race too, but that's only for adults.
Wow. How are you getting ready for it? Do you go to the gym?
I wanted to, but there isn't enough time. I cycle to school every day now, and on Sundays I ride with my uncle in the hills. That's the hardest part. I'm always really tired afterwards!
Have you got a good bike? Your old one's quite small, isn't it?
Yes, it's much too small now. So I'm borrowing my cousin's racing bike. It's really light and fast. Mum says if I do well, she'll buy me my own bike next year.
Is there a prize for the winner?
Yes, a hundred pounds and a medal. But I don't think I'll win. Some of the riders are in cycling clubs and they're really fast. I just want to finish in under an hour. That's my plan.
Can I come and watch?
Of course! It starts at the bridge at ten o'clock, but there are always lots of people there. My family's going to wait at the finish line in the park. You could come with them.
Great. I'll make a sign with your name on it!

script.t: We lost the match yesterday, sixty to forty-two.
Oh no. Were you upset?
Not really. The other team are much older than us, so we didn't expect to win. And I scored twelve points – my best ever! The coach said I played really well. I'm so happy with that.

items.intro: You will hear a girl talking about her school sports day.
items.q: What was the best thing about the day for her?

script.t: Sports day was great this year. I came third in the hundred metres, and I was quite happy with that. The weather was perfect too – sunny, but not too hot. But for me, the best part was the teachers' race at the end. Our maths teacher fell over, and everyone laughed – including him!

items.q: What does the girl say about golf?
options: It is harder than she thought.

script.t: How was your first golf lesson, Zara?
Fun, but I was terrible! It looks so easy when you watch it on TV. I hit the ground more times than the ball!
Will you go again?
Yes. The lessons are free for students, so why not?

part5.intro: You will hear Hannah talking to her grandfather about her friends. Which sport does each friend do at the sports centre?

script.t: So, Hannah, all your friends go to the new sports centre, don't they?
Yes, Grandpa, but we all do different things. Ruby used to play table-tennis, but she stopped because her back hurt. Now she plays volleyball with a team on Mondays.
And what about Tariq? Is he still mad about football?
He still watches it on TV, but the sports centre doesn't have a football team. So he plays hockey instead. He says it's faster.
Duc is the boy who lives near the lake, isn't he? I've seen him out on the water in a little boat.
Yes, his dad takes him sailing in the summer. But at the sports centre he goes swimming every day before school. He wants to swim in competitions.
Good for him. And Megan?
Megan's really tall, so everyone thought she'd play basketball. But she says she's terrible at catching the ball! She loves the skateboard park outside the centre. She's there every afternoon.
Skateboarding? Isn't that dangerous?
She always wears a helmet. And then there's Felix. His dad wanted him to play golf, like him, but Felix found it really boring. He joined the basketball club last month, and now he's in the team.
And what about you, Hannah?
Me? I'm still trying everything!
